<coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`)
  as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs (rule 14).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>



</system-reminder>

## /home/user/.factory/missions/e194b9e3-6a67-42b9-bfc9-dd4e1ac23b0c/planning-notes.md
# Planning notes for mission artifacts (orchestrator, 2026-10-22)

Read this before any other mission file. It records what the owner decided after `SPEC.md` v0.2 was
written, and the readiness facts the mission is built on. Where these notes and `SPEC.md` disagree,
these notes win (owner decisions after the spec); `SPEC.md` is amended as-built at the next
integration (RULES rule 8). Where these notes are silent, `SPEC.md` is the authority.

Repository: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory` (GitHub `dctellya/droid-observatory`).
Mission branch: `mission/observatory-v1` (created from `main` at `c8524c2`; pre-mission commit `2266d3e`).
Owner: David Carbajosa Tesoro (`dct`, GitHub `dctellya`).

## Files to read for context (all in the repository)

- `SPEC.md` (v0.2): §2 mission setup, §3 milestones S, M0–M5 with named tests and acceptance
  commands, §4 versions, §5 architecture, §6 tests, §7 CI, §8 deliverables.
- `ai/RULES.md` (binding), `AGENTS.md` (operational summary), `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` v0.6
  (FR ids, lanes, §7 event kinds, §10 metrics, appendix A canonical event).
- `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md` and
  `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md` (measured facts, pasted numbers).
- `config/observatory.example.toml`, `deny.toml`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`,
  `docs/decisions/*.md`.

## Owner decisions after SPEC v0.1 (2026-10-22), all binding

1. **Session file schema.** Droid session files carry no Droid version. The mapping version is
   selected from the Droid version recorded in the **fixture header** (`droid --version`, 0.247.0
   at capture). Token usage, model, tags and child linkage are read from the sibling
   `<session-id>.settings.json` (`tokenUsage`, `childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId`,
   `inclusiveTokenUsage`, `lastCallTokenUsage`, `assistantActiveTimeMs`, `tags`, `model`,
   `reasoningEffort`, `interactionMode`, `autonomyLevel`). Child sessions are sibling files linked by
   `session_start.callingSessionId` / `callingToolUseId`. JSONL `type` values seen: `message`,
   `todo_state`, `agent_turn_outcome`, `compaction_state`, `session_start`; `modelId`,
   `apiProvider`, `reasoningEffort` sit on assistant messages. Decision file at S integration; SPEC
   §3 M0 / §5.2 amended as-built then.
2. **Keyring.** `keyring-core` 1.0.1 + `apple-native-keyring-store` 1.0.2 (feature `keychain`,
   `set_default_store`) instead of `keyring` 4.x (fails `cargo deny`). Keychain items are generic
   passwords with service `droid-observatory/<name>` and account = the login user (`dct`), not the
   item name. Items present: `droid-observatory/github-token`, `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`.
   Decision file at S integration.
3. **DMG** only in the CI `bundle` job; local builds produce `.app` (`bundle.targets: ["app"]`).
4. **Tauri evidence.** Validators treat the Tauri window as a smoke check (process alive, `Running`
   log line, WebKit connections to port 3141, System Events lists the app). The browser surface
   (`trunk serve --port 3141` driven by `agent-browser`) is the primary interactive surface. At each
   milestone integration the owner takes one real screenshot with the display unlocked, attached to
   the report.
5. **Concurrency limits** (now SPEC §5.8 v0.2): max 3 concurrent agent-browser sessions per
   `trunk serve` (1.34–1.54 GB RSS each); `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10
   cores); all cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock; `trunk serve` and
   `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns 3141; cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s,
   incremental 1.46–2.08 s; `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
6. **GitHub token** is a fine-grained **read-only** PAT (Contents, Issues, Pull requests, Actions,
   Commit statuses, Metadata; repos droid-observatory and artstudio). No Checks permission: read
   check results through Actions runs (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs?head_sha=`) and commit
   statuses (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), never the check-runs API.
7. **M4 exit (supersedes SPEC §3 M4 acceptance "merge from the app").** Merge button is visible when
   the policy allows and checks are green; with the read-only token the app surfaces the 403 cleanly
   (clear message naming the PR, target and missing permission; no crash, no retry storm); the
   **owner** performs the merge (UI or API); the badge updates from the poll (`policy-merged` or
   `merged` as detected). The write-token question stays at the M3→M4 boundary.
8. **Throttling and caps.** At a Factory usage throttle (5-hour / 7-day / monthly limits) or at a
   milestone cap, the run pauses at the point reached, usage so far is written to
   `reports/usage/`, the stall flag goes up and the owner is asked. **No silent model or
   reasoning-effort downgrade, ever** (a change is a decision file, rule 19). The M0-boundary re-cap

# droid-observatory architecture

Authoritative design for the mission `observatory-v1`. Written for implementation workers (Rust,
Leptos, Tauri, CI) who will not read the PRD. Sources, in precedence order: `planning-notes.md`
(owner decisions after the spec, binding), `SPEC.md` v0.2, `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` v0.6,
`docs/decisions/D-*`, the two readiness reports of 2026-10-22, `config/observatory.example.toml`.
Where the sources leave a choice, the choice here is marked `[arch decision]` with its reason.
Paths are relative to the repository root unless absolute. Numbers are pasted from the readiness
reports; none are estimated.

## 1. System overview and invariants

A Factory Mission writes one JSONL per agent session under `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/`.
`observatory-core` turns those lines (and, later, a hosted JSON-RPC stream, local git and GitHub)
into canonical `Event`s on nine lanes, indexes them in SQLite by pointer, computes views and
metrics; `observatory-cli` exercises core headlessly; `observatory-app` (Tauri 2 shell + Leptos
CSR UI) renders the board. Attach (watch + tail) is the primary live mode; replay is attach at
end of file; host is the secondary path and the only one with a control channel (D-008).

Invariants every worker must keep (a violation is a blocking finding):

| # | Invariant | Where enforced |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | `observatory-core` is synchronous: no `tokio`, no `async fn` in its public API. tokio lives only in `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri`. | `cargo machete` + review; `Cargo.toml` of core has no async runtime |
| I2 | The UI holds no logic: card position, filters, scrubbing, tray count, details data, library entries are functions in `core::view`, unit-tested there. The Leptos crate only renders what the shell sends. | SPEC §6 "UI logic" |
| I3 | Raw lines are read-only and never copied into the store. The store keeps `path, byte_offset, byte_len`; the line is re-read on demand. `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written. | `store` DDL has no payload column; `JsonlSource` opens files read-only |
| I4 | Every `Event` carries `mapping_version` and a `SourcePtr`. | type system; test `every_event_carries_the_mapping_version()` |
| I5 | Unknown raw lines become `EventKind::Unknown { raw_type }`, are counted and shown (tray, CLI final line `unknown events: N`, exported counter), never dropped. | `mapping::map_record` is total: it always returns at least one `Event` |
| I6 | Thresholds and intervals come only from `Config` (`config/observatory.example.toml` is the contract); no literal in code. | `clippy.toml`; review |
| I7 | Secrets come only from the keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>`, account = login user) or, for the GitHub token only, `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Never in config, store, logs, telemetry, test fixtures. The `tracing` layer redacts (§12). | `secrets` module is the only reader |
| I8 | The one outward write is the merge (FR-G5), human-confirmed, named PR and target, logged as a lane-7 event. The app never merges on its own; `policy-merged` is observed, not performed. | `control::merge` is the only caller of `Forge::merge` |
| I9 | Core modules that the UI compiles to wasm (`model`, `mapping`, `view`, `metrics`, `config`) have no platform dependency; platform modules sit behind Cargo features (§2). | `trunk build` of the UI crate |

## 4. Ingest (`core::ingest`)

### 4.1 Source trait and RawRecord

```rust
pub struct RawRecord { pub ptr: SourcePtr, pub session_id: SessionId, pub bytes: Vec<u8> /* one line, no newline */ }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SourceKind { Jsonl, Rpc, Git, GitHub }

pub trait Source {
    fn kind(&self) -> SourceKind;
    /// Pull the next records. Returns an empty Vec when nothing new is available right now.
    /// Never blocks longer than one poll interval; never returns an error for "no data".
    fn next_batch(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<RawRecord>, IngestError>;
    /// True when every known file has been read to its current end (replay = attach that reached EOF, D-008).
    fn at_eof(&self) -> bool;
}
```

`[arch decision]` `next_batch` + `at_eof` replace SPEC §5.4's `poll`: the name says it pulls, and
`at_eof` is what makes replay and attach one code path (the CLI stops at `at_eof()`, the watcher keeps
calling). `IngestError` (thiserror): `Io { path, source }`, `FileMoved { path }`, `TooLarge { path, mb }`.

### 4.2 JsonlSource (S; sidecar and children M0)

```rust
pub struct JsonlSource { /* files: Vec<TailState { path, session_id, offset: u64, partial: Vec<u8> }>, cfg: IngestConfig */ }
impl JsonlSource {
    pub fn open(root: &Path, cfg: &IngestConfig) -> Result<Self, IngestError>;   // root = the orchestrator .jsonl
    pub fn add_file(&mut self, path: &Path) -> Result<SessionId, IngestError>;   // child or newly discovered file
    pub fn read_at(path: &Path, byte_offset: u64, byte_len: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>, IngestError>; // used by inspect/Details
}
```

Reading rules: open read-only; read from `offset` in chunks of `tail_chunk_kb`; split on `\n`; an
incomplete trailing fragment stays in `partial` until the newline arrives (a writer may be mid-line);
`byte_offset` is the offset of the first byte of the line, `byte_len` excludes the newline; a line
that is not valid JSON is still a `RawRecord` (mapping yields `Unknown { raw_type: "<unparseable>" }`).
Files over `max_session_file_mb` are indexed and a `TooLarge` warning is surfaced once.

### 4.3 Watcher (M1, feature `watch`)

```rust
pub struct SessionWatcher { /* notify::RecommendedWatcher + poll fallback */ }
impl SessionWatcher {
    pub fn start(cfg: &IngestConfig) -> Result<Self, IngestError>;  // scans cfg.factory_sessions_dir recursively
    pub fn next_discovered(&mut self) -> Vec<DiscoveredSession>;    // new *.jsonl since last call (notify or poll)
}
pub struct DiscoveredSession { pub path: PathBuf, pub session_id: SessionId, pub parent: Option<SessionId>,
                               pub name: String /* first tag, else session id (FR-L1) */ }
```

Design: `notify` 8.2.0 (FSEvents) for create/modify; a poll every `jsonl_poll_ms` (500) re-stats every
watched file and lists the directory, because FSEvents coalesces and a file created before start would be
missed (PRD §14). Startup scan attaches files modified in the last 24 h as growing [arch decision: a
bound so a directory with hundreds of old sessions does not open them all; older files stay in the
library and open on demand]. At most `max_watched_sessions` (64) files are tailed, newest first; the
UI shows "N sessions not watched". Growth is read by `JsonlSource::next_batch` in one `tail_chunk_kb`
step per poll. Everything runs on one `std::thread` owned by the shell (`backend.rs`), which batches
events toward the UI every `event_batch_ms` (100).

### 4.4 Capture header for live attach

`captures` row per attached directory: `id`, `source_dir`, `droid_version`, `started_at`. No file is
written next to Droid's files.

### 4.5 RpcSource (M2, feature `rpc`)

The shell spawns `droid exec --mission --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc
<flags from the launch screen> -f <mission file>` with `tokio::process` (stdin piped, stdout piped,
stderr to a log). Every stdout line is appended verbatim to the spool
`~/.droid-observatory/hosted/<launch-id>.jsonl` `[arch decision]`: a hosted stream exists nowhere else,
`inspect`/Details need a raw line, and the spool is the raw source for `SourcePtr::Rpc` (it is not a
copy of a Droid file). `RpcSource` is a `JsonlSource` over the spool (same tail code, I3 holds).
Control writes go to stdin as JSON-RPC 2.0 requests:

```rust
pub enum HostControl { Pause, Resume, Message { text: String }, Answer { question_id: String, text: String },
                       Approve { request_id: String }, Deny { request_id: String } }
pub struct RpcRequest { jsonrpc: "2.0", id: u64, method: String, params: serde_json::Value }
pub fn encode(c: &HostControl, id: u64) -> RpcRequest;   // method names are confirmed in M2 from `droid exec --help`
                                                         // and the first hosted capture; recorded in the M2 decision file
```

An acknowledgement is the JSON-RPC response with the same `id`; `pause_request_is_written_as_jsonrpc_and_acknowledged()`
asserts it. The child is in its own process group and is killed on window close
(`child_process_is_reaped_on_window_close()`); the readiness report shows why: killing the parent alone
orphans children (`trunk serve` and the app binary reparented to PID 1 in the Tauri run).

```rust
    fn policy(&self, target: &str) -> Result<MergePolicy, ForgeError>; // rulesets + branch protection
    fn reviews(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Review>, ForgeError>;
    fn attestations(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Attestation>, ForgeError>;
    fn merge(&self, pr: &Pr, method: MergeMethod) -> Result<Merged, ForgeError>;
}
pub struct Pr { pub number: u64, pub head_sha: String, pub head: String, pub base: String, pub url: String,
                pub state: PrState /* Open, Merged { by: MergedBy::Human | Policy, at }, Closed */ }
pub struct Check { pub name: String, pub source: CheckSource /* ActionsRun { run_id } | CommitStatus { context } */,
                   pub conclusion: CheckConclusion /* Queued, Running, Passed, Failed, RequiredMissing */, pub url: String }
pub struct MergePolicy { pub requires_human: bool, pub allowed_methods: Vec<MergeMethod>,
                         pub decided_by: RuleAttribution /* Ruleset { id, name } | BranchProtection | ConfigOverride(String) | NoRule */ }
pub enum ForgeError { Forbidden { pr: u64, target: String, missing_permission: &'static str /* "pull_requests:write" */ },
                      RateLimited { reset_at }, Http { status, url }, Other(String) }
```

`GitHubSource` uses the token from `secrets::github_token()` (§12), base `https://api.github.com`,
endpoints: `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls?head={o}:{branch}&base={target}&state=all`,
`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs?head_sha=`, `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`,
`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rules/branches/{target}` and `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets`,
`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/branches/{target}/protection` (404 → no protection),
`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews`, `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/attestations/{subject-digest}` (best effort),
`PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/merge`. The check-runs API is never called (planning note 6). Poll every
`[github].poll_interval_s` (30). HTTP client: `ureq` 3 (blocking, rustls) `[arch decision]`: core has
no tokio (I1); version verified on the day with `make deny`. `GitSource` runs `git` via
`std::process::Command` in the repository: `for-each-ref refs/heads/mission/*`, `worktree list --porcelain`,
`log --first-parent --merges mission/<name>` for integration commits → `IntegrationMerged`; fast-check
runs come from `GET /actions/runs?branch=mission/<name>` → `GateCommandRun/Passed/Failed` attributed to
the milestone whose `wt/<m>` merge commit is the run's head.

Target branch comes from `[github].target_branch` (default `"main"`, §11); the mission branch from
`[mission].branch_pattern`. Merge policy: `[github].merge_policy = "auto"` reads GitHub (`requires_human`
= ruleset/protection requires a PR and no auto-merge is enabled); `"human"` forces the button;
`"policy"` never shows it (`decided_by = ConfigOverride`). Gate badge state machine (`view::gate`):
`Pending` (no PR) → `ChecksRunning` → `ReviewRequested` | `HumanRequired` | `RulesetBlocked` | `CiRed` →
`CiGreen` → `PolicyMerged` | `MergedByHuman`. `PolicyMerged` is set when the poll sees `state = Merged`
with no app merge action in `human_actions` for that PR (`policy_merged_detected_without_human_action()`).

Merge button flow (planning note 7): visible only when `requires_human && all required checks Passed`
(`merge_button_shows_only_when_policy_is_human_and_checks_are_green()`); click → confirmation dialog
naming `PR #n` and `target`; confirm → `control::merge` writes the lane-7 `PrMergedByHuman` intent row
with `state = requested`, calls `Forge::merge`; on `ForgeError::Forbidden` the UI shows exactly
`Merge of PR #<n> into <target> refused: token lacks <missing_permission>. Merge in GitHub; the badge
updates from the next poll.`; no retry, the row becomes `state = refused`, the button stays visible, the
poll continues at the normal interval (no storm). The owner merges; the next poll yields `PolicyMerged`
or `MergedByHuman` depending on the merger login equalling the token owner.

## 9. Metrics (`core::metrics`, M5)

Time states (PRD §10.1): `enum TimeState { Active, WaitingHuman(Question|Permission|Merge), WaitingValidation,
RetryFailure, IdleQueued, IdleUnscheduled }`. `pub fn partition(events_of_feature: &[Event], end: Timestamp)
-> Vec<Interval { from, to, state }>`, contiguous and non-overlapping
(`time_states_partition_every_instant_exactly_once()`). Active intervals `[arch decision]`: each event
with `duration` contributes `[at, at + duration]`; `duration` is set by the mapper as `tool_result.at -
tool_use.at` for tool calls and `assistant.at - previous_line.at` (same session) for model generation.
`ToolError`/`HookBlocked` intervals are `RetryFailure`; an open `QuestionAsked`/`PermissionRequested`/
green-but-unmerged gate with no active interval is `WaitingHuman`; `TaskDone` without a validator start is
`WaitingValidation`; a defined feature blocked by another's active interval is `IdleQueued`, else
`IdleUnscheduled`. The oracle (below) validates these rules.

Rework windows (`metrics::rework`): open/close pairs from PRD §10.2 (`FindingBlocking→ReworkResolved`,
`QaScenarioFailed→QaScenarioPassed` same scenario, `IntegrationConflict→IntegrationConflictResolved`,
`CheckFailed→CheckPassed` same check); overlapping windows on one feature merge; unresolved at mission end
reported with `closed_by = None`. Causes: `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate`.
Overhead (`metrics::overhead`): orchestrator intervals before the first `FeatureDefined`, replanning not
attributable, and compaction recovery; reported as its own line; `[metrics].overhead_apportionment =
"equal"` splits it and labels the output `apportioned`. Derived (`metrics::derived`): cycle (feature,
milestone, mission, per lane), waste by the 8 SPEC §5.6 causes, bottleneck (lane/role with highest
waiting + queued; lane with highest WIP/throughput), fix loops (count of `fix` cycles).

Cost (`metrics::cost`): tokens from `UsageReported` (sidecar `tokenUsage`); credits primary when
`factoryCredits` is present; otherwise `Σ tokens × per_m / 1e6` from `config/prices/<date>.toml`
(`[metrics].price_table`); every `Cost` carries `price_table: String` (the `effective` date)
(`cost_names_the_price_table_date()`). Budget meter: `[metrics].budget` or the launch `budget_usd`.
Model comparison (FR-M7): per role, per model, `cost_per_completed_feature` and
`first_pass_active_s_per_completed_feature`.

Oracle (`tests/oracle.rs`, `reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv`, owner-produced before M5).
Column contract `[arch decision]` (fixed now so the owner can produce it):

```text
scope,id,name,cycle_s,first_pass_active_s,rework_s,waste_waiting_human_question_s,waste_waiting_human_permission_s,
waste_waiting_merge_s,waste_waiting_validation_s,waste_rework_s,waste_retry_failure_s,waste_idle_queued_s,
waste_idle_unscheduled_s,rework_windows,tokens_input,tokens_output,tokens_cache_read,tokens_cache_write,cost_usd,price_table
```

`scope ∈ {feature, milestone}`; durations integer seconds; tolerance 1 s, 1 token, 0.01 USD
(`metrics_match_reference_spreadsheet_within_tolerance()`). `observatory-cli metrics <root.jsonl> --csv`
prints exactly these columns; `--json` prints `MetricsReport`. Export (`metrics::export`): same rows to

1→# droid-observatory — Spec for the mission
2→
3→Owner: David Carbajosa (architect, reviewer, the human in lane 7). Implementers: one Factory
4→Mission (orchestrator, workers, validators) under ai/RULES.md. Status: v0.1 approved by the owner
5→(2026-10-22); v0.2: §5.8 concurrency limits added (owner decision 2026-10-22). Living document: §9 is the human feedback channel, §10 the as-built history.

7→Inputs: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` (v0.5), `ai/prd/review-2026-10-22.md`, `ai/RULES.md`,
8→`ai/SPEC-TEMPLATE.md`, `docs/decisions/D-001..D-010`, `BACKLOG.md`, `config/observatory.example.toml`,
9→`config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md` entries 17–21.
10→
11→Approval boundary: this document is the contract the mission plans from. Until the owner answers
12→`approved`, nothing else happens: no milestone plan, no worktree, no application code, no GitHub
13→object. After approval the mission plans from this file only (rule 9: deviations are proposed with
14→reason and cost, and wait).
15→
16→## 1. Purpose
17→
18→**What it is.** A Rust desktop application (Tauri 2 shell, Leptos UI, `observatory-core` library)
19→that shows one Factory Mission moving through nine lanes (PRD §7): Intent, Orchestrator, Workers,
20→Validators-scrutiny, Validators-user-testing, Integration, Human, Outside, and Time/Waste/Cost/models.
21→Cards are milestones with their features inside (PRD §8); every lane entry is a view over the raw
22→JSONL line it came from, never a copy (PRD §11.2).
23→
24→**For whom.** The mission owner who runs missions from a terminal and wants to see flow and cost;
25→the reviewer who opens Details and merges; the engineering lead who compares models over time
26→(PRD §6). Single user, local data, the user's own GitHub access.
27→
28→**What it must prove.** The mission is done when all of these hold on the mission branch:
29→
30→1. **Attach.** A mission started from any terminal on this machine appears on the board and every
31→   event of it shows within 1 s (FR-L1, FR-B6), with no control channel.
32→2. **Replay with a frozen mapping.** `observatory-cli replay` over the frozen capture ends with
33→   `unknown events: 0`, and the board renders the same capture with correct lane positions
34→   (FR-L2, FR-B7, rule 18).
35→3. **Host.** A mission launched from the app shows events within 1 s and the pause, message and
36→   answer controls reach the orchestrator (FR-L3, FR-H1..H4).
37→4. **Gate and fix loop.** Against the demo branch pair in this repository (§3 M4): a red check
38→   opens a `fix` cycle on the affected card, a green check with a human policy shows Merge, and
39→   merging from the app flips the badge (FR-G3..G8).
40→5. **Time, waste, cost.** Metrics recomputed from the frozen capture match the owner's reference
41→   spreadsheet within rounding (FR-M1..M7, PRD §10); every cost names its price-table date.
42→6. **The build is the first dataset.** The sessions of this mission are the capture that M0
43→   freezes and M5 is measured against (rule 17).
44→
45→**Out of scope (explicit).** PRD §5 non-goals: planning inside the app, multi-user or server
46→deployment, writing to Factory's hosted API beyond what `droid` does, editing or reviewing code in
47→the app, CI systems other than GitHub Actions. Also out: CI telemetry to Grafana (B-002), a
48→dedicated error tracker (B-003), Linux and Windows bundles (macOS is the target; the devcontainer
49→is core-only, B-001), the app performing any merge other than the human-confirmed Merge button
50→(FR-G5): v1 never merges on its own. Observing a merge performed by a ruleset or a bot stays in
51→scope: the gate badge shows `policy-merged` on detection (FR-G6, M4). Also out: a second mapping
52→version for Droid releases newer than the one captured. Guard: the mapper is versioned from day
53→one, every `Event` carries `mapping_version`, and the unknown-event count is always visible (tray,
54→CLI summary, exported series), so the first Droid upgrade shows as a rising count, never as a
55→silently broken board. And out: migrating the backlog before the mission starts (entry 19).
56→
57→**What this spec answers.** The review note `ai/prd/review-2026-10-22.md` item 5 (attach is the
58→primary live mode, D-008). The owner decisions logged after PRD v0.5: the telemetry contract and
59→series budget (D-010, B-017, §5.7), M4 on a demo branch pair in this repository instead of a
60→private demo repository (entry 19, B-007, §3 M4), the hybrid backlog driven by the mission
61→(entry 19, §8), the orchestrator model id `claude-fable-5.1` (entry 21, D-006 correction, §2),
62→and the backlog items the spec session owns: B-005 (§6), B-010 (§3), B-014 (§7), B-017 (§5.7).
63→
64→## 2. Mission setup
65→
66→**Command** (run by the owner from the repository root on a checkout of `main` that contains this
67→approved spec; the mission creates `mission/observatory-v1` from it):
68→
69→```sh
70→droid exec --mission --auto high \
71→  --model claude-fable-5.1          --reasoning-effort high \
72→  --worker-model claude-sonnet-5-5  --worker-reasoning-effort high \
73→  --validator-model claude-opus-5-5 --validator-reasoning-effort high \
74→  --output-format text \
75→  -f SPEC.md
76→```
77→
78→| Flag | Value | Reason |
79→|---|---|---|
80→| `--mission --auto high` | required | Missions auto-approve proposals and need `--auto high` (Droid 0.247.0 `droid exec --help`). The hooks in `.factory/hooks.json` are the guard, not the prompt. |
81→| `--model` | `claude-fable-5.1` | Orchestrator (D-006, corrected 2026-10-22 from the misspelt `claude-fable-5-1`, which fell back to GPT-6 Sol). Factory catalog id, 4× multiplier. |
82→| `--reasoning-effort` | `high` | Fable's default; planning and integration are where judgment is bought. `xhigh`/`max` on a 4× model is not justified before a measured need. |
83→| `--worker-model` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | Workers (D-006). 0.8× multiplier. Catalog id per docs.factory.com/models; `droid exec --help` on this machine lists `claude-sonnet-5` but not `claude-sonnet-5-5`; owner confirmed available on 2026-10-22. |
84→| `--worker-reasoning-effort` | `high` | Owner decision 2026-10-22: the model default; Rust compile errors and Leptos (little training data, PRD §12) need the reasoning. The cost/quality split lane 9 measures is between models, not efforts. |
85→| `--validator-model` | `claude-opus-5-5` | Validators, scrutiny and user testing (D-006). 1.6× multiplier. |
86→| `--validator-reasoning-effort` | `high` | Above Opus's default `medium`: validation is where correctness is bought (D-006 alternatives). |
87→| `--output-format` | `text` | The terminal is for the human; the dataset is the session JSONL under `~/.factory/sessions/`, which attach and replay read. |
88→| `-f SPEC.md` | this file | The mission plans from the approved spec (template, last paragraph). |

91→Factory App uses them: `missionOrchestratorModel`, `missionOrchestratorReasoningEffort`,
92→`missionModelSettings.workerModel`, `.workerReasoningEffort`, `.validationWorkerModel`,
93→`.validationWorkerReasoningEffort`. The three reasoning-effort keys are added with the spec PR
94→(§8). A change to any model is a decision file (rule 19).
95→
96→**Mission branch.** `mission/observatory-v1`, created from `main` at the commit that contains this
97→approved spec. One pull request `mission/observatory-v1` → `main` at the end of the mission, opened
98→by the orchestrator, merged by the human after `gate` is green. Nothing else reaches `main`
99→(rule 12). The branch is deleted at the merge (PRD §2).

101→**Worktree policy.** One worktree per milestone: `git worktree add ../observatory-wt/<m> -b wt/<m>
102→mission/observatory-v1` where `<m>` is `s`, `m0` … `m5`. Workers and validators of a milestone
103→work only inside its worktree. Two worktrees never edit the same file (rule 13); the shared files
104→(`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md`, `reports/`) are written by
105→the orchestrator on the mission branch at integration. Integration is `git merge --no-ff wt/<m>`
106→into `mission/observatory-v1` by the orchestrator, then `make check` locally, then the
107→`mission-checks` run on the push must be green before the next milestone starts. A worktree is
108→removed after integration; its branch stays (history).
109→
110→**Gate command.** `make check` is the only local gate: it is exactly what `mission-branch.yml`
111→runs (rule 5). A worker hands off only with `make check` green in its worktree; the orchestrator
112→integrates only with `make check` green on the mission branch.
113→
114→**Hooks that must be active.** `.factory/hooks.json`: `guard-git.sh` (PreToolUse on `Execute`,

116→appends one JSON line per tool call to `build-log/<UTC-day>/<session>.jsonl`). Git hooks via
117→`make hooks` (`core.hooksPath=.githooks`): `pre-commit` (gitleaks on staged files, file size, debt
118→markers, decisions index, rustfmt, markdownlint), `commit-msg` (subject ≤ 72 chars, no WIP/fixup),
119→`pre-push` (no `main`, no non-fast-forward). A worker that finds a hook missing stops and reports;
120→it never disables or bypasses one (`--no-verify` is a rule 12 violation).
121→
122→**Usage budget per milestone.** Unit: USD-equivalent at `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, computed
123→from the token counts Factory reports for the mission's sessions (the usage page or the stream's
124→`usage.reported`), pasted into `reports/usage/<milestone>.md` at integration (rule 7). Factory
125→Standard Credits are recorded next to it when visible. The caps below are the owner's planning
126→numbers, not measurements; this is the first mission and there is no prior run to calibrate on.
127→At the M0 boundary the orchestrator proposes re-caps for M1–M5 from the measured S and M0 usage
128→(owner decision 2026-10-22); until then the table stands.
129→
130→| Milestone | Cap (USD-eq) | Reason for the size |
131→|---|---|---|
132→| S  walking skeleton | 40 | Thin slice, few files, mostly scaffolding and one fixture. |
133→| M0 capture and mapping | 60 | Mapper plus golden tests; the capture already exists (§3 M0). |
134→| M1 board, replay, attach | 150 | Largest UI milestone and the Leptos go/no-go; rework budget inside. |
135→| M2 host | 80 | RPC adapter plus launch screen; the control channel is new ground. |
136→| M3 intervention | 60 | Lane-7 semantics over M2 controls; small surface. |
137→| M4 branch, gate, fix loop | 120 | Two adapters (git, GitHub), the demo branch pair, a live PR loop. |
138→| M5 time, waste, cost | 120 | The metric engine and its oracle test; export; charts. |
139→| Total | 630 | Hard stop for the mission; the final PR and fixes come out of the unspent remainder. |
140→
141→At a cap the orchestrator stops dispatching, writes the usage so far to `reports/usage/`, raises
142→the stall flag and waits for the human (rule 15). Spending beyond a cap is a deviation (rule 9).
143→
144→**What the human will answer mid-mission.** Only at a milestone boundary or when the stall flag is
145→up (rule 15): the M1 go/no-go (PRD §12), a budget cap reached, a proposed deviation from this spec
146→with its reason and cost, a keychain item or GitHub permission the mission cannot create itself
147→(§3 M4, §5.9), the reference spreadsheet for M5 (B-008), and a red `gate` on the final PR.
148→
149→**What the human will not answer.** Style, naming, crate choice within §4, test structure, how to
150→split a milestone into features, which worker does what, or anything already decided here or in
151→`docs/decisions/`. Those go to the backlog with a reason or into a decision file (rules 13, 14).

153→## 3. Milestones
154→
155→Seven milestones on the board of the build: the walking skeleton `S` first (rule 2), then
156→`M0`–`M5` in PRD §13 order. PRD §13 counts six; the seventh is the skeleton rule 2 requires, so
157→the PRD count is superseded here (rule 8). A milestone is integrated into the mission branch, never
158→shipped. The spec itself is not a milestone: it is approved before the mission starts.

386→## 5. Architecture
387→
388→Each decision carries its reason. Numbers come from the PRD and `config/observatory.example.toml`
389→unless a reason says otherwise.
390→
391→### 5.1 Crates and interfaces
392→
393→| Crate / app | Responsibility | Public interface | Reason |
394→|---|---|---|---|
395→| `crates/observatory-core` | ingest, model, mapping, store, metrics, control, telemetry; **no UI dependency, sync, no tokio** | `Source` trait, `Event`, `Store`, `Metrics`, `Control`, `Config` | Testable from fixtures alone; every milestone's logic lives here so the UI can be swapped (PRD §12 go/no-go). |
396→| `crates/observatory-cli` | headless `replay`, `inspect`, `attach --watch`, `metrics --csv` over core | `observatory-cli <cmd>` | Rule 2: the first thing that works; rule 5: what CI runs; the validators' oracle for every milestone. |
397→| `apps/observatory-app` | Tauri 2 shell (`src-tauri`) + Leptos CSR UI (`src`) | Tauri commands and events, serde types imported from core | One language, no bindings drift (PRD §12). Commands are the only boundary the UI crosses, so a TypeScript UI could replace it without touching core. |
398→
399→Tauri commands (M1 onward): `open_replay(path)`, `list_sessions()`, `attach(session_id)`,
400→`event_raw(ptr)`, `host_launch(cfg)`, `host_control(cmd)`, `metrics(scope)`, `gate(mission)`,
401→`merge(pr, target)`, `telemetry_status()`. Events from shell to UI: `events_appended(batch)`,
402→`session_discovered`, `stall_flag`, `gate_changed`. Batches flush every 100 ms (reason: well under
403→the 1 s requirement, avoids one render per line).
404→
405→### 5.2 Canonical event and lane mapping
406→
407→`Event`, `ReworkWindow`, `Lane`, `Role`, `EventKind` as in PRD appendix A; `EventKind` has one
408→variant per PRD §7 kind in `CamelCase` plus `Unknown { raw_type }`. `source: SourcePtr::Jsonl {
409→path, byte_offset, byte_len }` (appendix A has `path, byte_offset`; `byte_len` is added so a line
410→can be read without scanning for the newline) is the only thing the store keeps of a raw line
411→(PRD §11.2: the lane is a view). `mapping_version: MappingVersion` is a second addition to
412→appendix A: every `Event` names the mapper that produced it, so the first Droid upgrade shows as a
413→rising unknown-event count against a known version, never as a silently broken board (owner,
414→entry 23). Mapping is a module `mapping::v1` with a `MappingVersion`
415→selected from the Droid version in the session `.settings.json`; unknown Droid versions use the
416→latest mapping and raise a one-line warning (reason: an old capture must keep replaying, rule 18
417→covers the rest). A mapping version is frozen at M0 and never edited; a later Droid release gets
418→`mapping::v2` and its own fixture. The golden file `fixtures/streams/<capture>.events.json` is the
419→contract of a version.
420→

422→
423→SQLite via `rusqlite` with the `bundled` feature (reason: core is sync, a desktop index needs no
424→async driver, and bundling removes the system-library dependency from the clean-clone rule).
425→File: `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite` (schema version table, migrations forward-only).
426→
427→| Table | Columns (keys) | Note |
428→|---|---|---|
429→| `sessions` | `id`, `path`, `droid_version`, `tag`, `role`, `parent_id`, `mission_id`, `started_at`, `ended_at` | One row per JSONL file; `tag` confirmed in M0 |
430→| `events` | `id`, `session_id`, `mission_id`, `milestone_id`, `feature_id`, `lane`, `kind`, `raw_type`, `mapping_version`, `role`, `model`, `at`, `duration_ms`, `path`, `byte_offset`, `byte_len` | Pointer, never payload |
431→| `usage` | `event_id`, `input`, `output`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`, `credits` | From `usage.reported` |
432→| `missions`, `milestones`, `features` | ids, names, `defined_at`, `completed_at`, `state` | Board model |
433→| `rework_windows` | `feature_id`, `opened_by`, `closed_by`, `cause` | PRD §10.2 |
434→| `prs`, `checks`, `attestations`, `reviews` | GitHub ids, state, `observed_at`, `url` | Lane 8 |
435→| `human_actions` | `id`, `kind`, `target`, `at`, `payload_ptr` | Lane 7 |
436→| `prices` | `effective`, `model`, `class`, `per_m`, `source` | Loaded from the dated TOML |
437→| `mapping_versions` | `version`, `droid_version_range`, `frozen_at` | §5.2 |

440→shows the pointer (reason: never copy raw lines, PRD §11.2).

442→### 5.4 Ingest adapters behind traits
443→
444→```rust
445→pub trait Source { fn poll(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<RawRecord>>; fn kind(&self) -> SourceKind; }
446→pub trait Forge  { fn pr(&self, branch: &str, target: &str) -> Result<Option<Pr>>;
447→                   fn checks(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Check>>; fn policy(&self, target: &str) -> Result<MergePolicy>;
448→                   fn merge(&self, pr: &Pr, method: MergeMethod) -> Result<Merged>; /* attestations, reviews */ }
449→```
450→
451→`JsonlSource` (attach; replay = the same source at end of file with a clock the scrubber drives),
452→`RpcSource` (host, M2), `GitSource` (M4), `GitHubSource: Forge` (M4). Reason: one adapter for
453→attach and replay removes a whole class of "works in replay, not live" bugs (D-008); the `Forge`
454→trait is the seam for other forges later (PRD §5 non-goal, §11.2).
455→
456→### 5.5 Config keys with defaults
457→
458→Everything in `config/observatory.example.toml` as committed (`[mission]`, `[ingest]`, `[github]`,
459→`[intervention]`, `[metrics]`, `[telemetry]`), with these additions the mission makes, each with
460→its reason in the file (rule 4):
461→
462→| Key | Default | Reason |
463→|---|---|---|
464→| `[ingest].max_watched_sessions` | 64 | Bounds file handles and tail threads on a laptop; beyond it the newest are watched and the UI says how many are not. |
465→| `[ingest].max_session_file_mb` | 512 | Larger files are indexed but tail reads warn; protects memory on runaway sessions. |
466→| `[ingest].tail_chunk_kb` | 1024 | Read size per tail step; one chunk per poll keeps latency under 1 s at typical mission output rates. |
467→| `[ui].event_batch_ms` | 100 | Shell→UI flush interval (§5.1). |
468→| `[ui].dev_port` | 3141 | `trunk serve` port for the browser host used by validators (§6); chosen outside common dev ranges, confirmed free at planning. |
469→| `[store].path` | `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite` | One index per user; raw lines stay where Droid wrote them. |
470→| `[telemetry].max_milestone_labels` | 8 | 7 named milestones of this mission plus one `overflow` value; bounds the `milestone` label for any observed mission (§5.7). |
471→| `[telemetry].mission_switch_min_interval_min` | 30 | The exported mission changes at most twice an hour, so two missions' series never count as active together (§5.7). |
472→| `[telemetry].buckets.mission_cycle_seconds` | `[3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 86400, 172800]` | Missions run hours to days. |
473→| `[telemetry].buckets.feature_cycle_seconds` | `[600, 1800, 3600, 7200, 14400]` | Features run minutes to hours. |
474→
475→### 5.6 Metric definitions
476→
477→By reference, not restated: time states PRD §10.1, rework windows §10.2, mission overhead §10.3,
478→cycle/waste/bottleneck/fix loops §10.4, cost §10.5. Closed cause lists used by the engine and the
479→exporter: **waste causes** `waiting_human_question`, `waiting_human_permission`, `waiting_merge`,
480→`waiting_validation`, `rework`, `retry_failure`, `idle_queued`, `idle_unscheduled` (8);
481→**rework causes** `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate` (4). Mission overhead is a
482→separate line in the app and is not exported (reason: it belongs to no card and D-010 has no label
483→for it). The CSV export has one row per feature with every §10.4 measure and the price-table date.
484→
485→### 5.7 Telemetry series budget (D-010, B-017)
486→
487→Contract: OTLP `http/protobuf` to `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp`; header
488→value only from the keychain item `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`; resource attributes
489→`service.name=droid-observatory`, `service.version`; labels only from `mission`, `milestone`,
490→`role`, `model`, `cause`; counters and histograms only; one mission exported at a time.
491→
492→| Metric | Instrument | Labels | Cardinality (worst case) | Series |
493→|---|---|---|---|---|
494→| `observatory.mission.cycle_seconds` | histogram, 6 buckets | `mission` | 1 × (6 + `+Inf` + `_sum` + `_count`) | 9 |
495→| `observatory.feature.cycle_seconds` | histogram, 5 buckets | `mission` | 1 × (5 + 3) | 8 |
496→| `observatory.waste_seconds` | counter | `mission`, `milestone`, `cause` | 8 milestones × 8 causes | 64 |
497→| `observatory.rework_windows` | counter | `mission`, `milestone`, `cause` | 8 × 4 | 32 |
498→| `observatory.fix_loops` | counter | `mission`, `milestone` | 8 | 8 |
499→| `observatory.tokens.{input,output,cache_read,cache_write}` | 4 counters | `mission`, `role`, `model` | 3 roles × 4 models = 12 pairs × 4 | 48 |
500→| `observatory.cost_usd` | counter | `mission`, `role`, `model` | 12 | 12 |
501→| `observatory.unknown_events` | counter | `mission` | 1 | 1 |
502→| **Total worst case** | | | | **182** |
503→
504→Expected for this mission (7 milestones, 3 role×model pairs): 9 + 8 + 56 + 28 + 7 + 12 + 3 + 1 =
505→**124**. Both are strictly under 200. Why these shapes: the feature-cycle histogram carries no
506→`milestone` label because a histogram per milestone (7 series each) would cost 56 series for a
507→distribution the app already shows per card; waste and rework keep `milestone` because the budget
508→meter and the waste chart are read per card. Guards: the `milestone` label is bounded by
509→`max_milestone_labels` (the ninth and later milestones of any observed mission export as
510→`milestone="overflow"`); `role` is the closed `Role` enum; `model` beyond four distinct values per
511→mission exports as `model="other"`; the exporter refuses to start if its computed worst case for the
512→configured buckets and limits is not under `[telemetry].max_series`, and the test
513→`exported_series_count_is_under_budget_on_worst_case_labels()` pins the 182. Series of a previous
514→mission stop being written when the export target changes; `mission_switch_min_interval_min` keeps
515→the two sets from overlapping inside Grafana's active-series window. A `service.version` change
516→(release) re-keys the resource once; it is not a steady-state cost. CI telemetry stays deferred
517→(B-002). D-010 sized the shape at up to 6 milestones; this spec uses 8 label values because the
518→skeleton makes seven milestones and one `overflow` value bounds other missions. Still under 200.
519→
520→### 5.8 Runtime limits
521→
522→From §5.5: 64 watched sessions, 512 MB per session file before warnings, 1 MiB tail chunk,
523→100 ms UI batch, 500 ms JSONL poll, 30 s GitHub poll, 15 s metric export, 20 min stall threshold.
524→The UI holds at most the visible window of events; everything else is a store query (reason: a
525→mission can emit tens of thousands of lines; the board must stay at 60 fps on a laptop). The host
526→child process is reaped on window close (M2 test). No network access except GitHub (when a token
527→is present) and the OTLP gateway (when enabled); both are shown in a status bar.
528→
529→Validation and build concurrency (measured 2026-10-22; source:
530→`reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`):
531→
532→- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
533→  CPU negligible idle).
534→- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
535→- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
536→  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`).
537→- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141.
538→- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
539→
540→### 5.9 Security
541→
542→- Secrets only from the macOS keychain or the environment (rule 4): `droid-observatory/github-token`
543→  or `GITHUB_TOKEN` for lane 8; `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` for telemetry (no environment
544→  fallback in the app, D-010). Never in config, store, logs or the exported telemetry.
545→- Raw JSONL is rendered read-only after the B-006 scrub pass, never uploaded, never copied into the
546→  store (PRD §11.2); rendering read-only and the merge as the one outward write are PRD §11.3.
547→  Fixtures are committed only after gitleaks and a human read (§3).
548→- The one outward write is the merge (FR-G5): confirmation names PR number and target branch;
549→  the app uses the repository's allowed merge method; the action is a lane-7 event.
550→- Telemetry carries no session id, event id, feature id or free text (D-010); the label allow-list
551→  is enforced in code and by test.
552→
553→## 6. Tests
554→
555→Fixtures are captured streams, named and dated (§3). Local = `make check` in a worktree; MB = the
556→`mission-checks` aggregate on `mission/**`; PR = the `gate` aggregate on the final pull request.
557→
558→| Suite | Covers | Where | Command |
559→|---|---|---|---|
560→| Unit (`#[cfg(test)]` next to code) | model, mapping helpers, time-state engine, windows, cost, label allow-list | local, MB, PR | `cargo test --workspace --all-features` |
561→| Fixture replay (`crates/observatory-core/tests/replay_*.rs`, `mapping.rs`) | each fixture → golden lane events, `unknown events: 0` on frozen captures | local, MB, PR | `make replay-fixtures`; `cargo test -p observatory-core --test mapping` |
562→| Attach latency (`tests/attach_latency.rs`) | harness appends a fixture line by line; event visible to the store within 1 s | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-core --test attach_latency` |
563→| CLI (`crates/observatory-cli/tests/cli.rs`) | exit codes, `unknown events: N` line, `inspect` prints the exact raw line | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-cli` |
564→| Metrics oracle (`tests/oracle.rs`, M5) | engine output vs `reports/reference/*.csv` within tolerance | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-core --test oracle` |
565→| Telemetry budget (M5) | worst-case series count = 182 < 200; labels outside the set rejected | local, MB, PR | part of unit |
566→| UI logic | view-model functions (card position, filters, scrubber) live in core and are unit-tested there; the Leptos layer holds no logic worth a wasm test runner (reason: `wasm-bindgen-test` adds a toolchain step for little coverage) | local, MB, PR | part of unit |
567→| Interactive QA (validators) | board, Details, tray, filters, scrubber in the **browser host** `trunk serve --port 3141` with the fixture opened through the file picker; attach, host, controls and gate in the **Tauri window** (`make app-dev`) with screenshots and the CLI as oracle | per milestone, by the user-testing validator | `make app-dev`; `trunk serve --port 3141` |
568→| Coverage (B-005) | `observatory-core` lines | S: reported; **M0 onward: fail under 80 %**; MB and PR | `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80` |
569→
570→**B-005 settled: 80 % lines on `observatory-core`.** Reason: core holds every piece of logic that
571→can be wrong silently (mapping, time states, cost), so it is where coverage buys correctness;
572→IO adapters that need a live `droid` or GitHub are in core too and cannot all be exercised in CI,
573→which is the 20 % of room. The CLI is thin and covered by its own tests without a threshold; the
574→UI crate is excluded (wasm target, no logic). Enforced from M0 integration because S has too little
575→code for a percentage to mean anything. Raising it is a backlog item with a reason, lowering it is
576→a decision file.
577→
578→## 7. CI
579→
580→Two workflows, one required check (D-003). Measured per run; the wall time of the aggregate is
581→pasted into `reports/ci/<date>-<milestone>.md` at integration (rule 11).
582→
583→**Mission branch** (`mission-branch.yml`, on push and PR to `mission/**`; aggregate
584→`mission-checks`; budget 3 min warm): markdownlint, lychee, actionlint, file size, debt markers,
585→decisions index, gitleaks, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`,
586→`make replay-fixtures`, `cargo deny check`, plus from S: **`cargo machete`** (B-014) and
587→**`cargo llvm-cov` with the §6 threshold** (B-005). Independent jobs in parallel with the
588→rust-cache. Gates integration: the orchestrator waits for green before the next milestone. If the
589→warm time exceeds 3 min after the coverage job joins, coverage moves to the final PR only, by
590→decision file.
591→
592→**B-014 settled: `cargo-machete`, not `cargo-udeps`.** Reason: machete runs on the stable toolchain
593→in seconds; udeps needs nightly, which is a second toolchain to pin and cache for a check that
594→finds a strict superset only in edge cases. Revisit if machete misses a real unused dependency.
595→
596→**Demo gate** (`demo-gate.yml`, M4, on `pull_request` to `demo/base`): one job that fails when the
597→label `demo:red` is present. Required by the `demo-gate` ruleset on `demo/base` only. Never touches
598→`main`.
599→
600→**Final pull request** (`gate.yml`, on PR to `main`; aggregate `gate`, the only check the `main`
601→ruleset requires): everything above plus Semgrep (SARIF to code scanning), Trivy filesystem scan of
602→the repository (vuln, misconfig, secret; HIGH and CRITICAL; `Cargo.lock` is what makes the vuln
603→scan meaningful), Checkov on the workflows, SBOM (`syft`), the macOS Tauri bundle (`bundle.yml`)
604→with build provenance (`attest-build-provenance`) and cosign signatures, Trivy results and SBOM
605→attached as artifacts. It never deploys. `release.yml` on `v*` tags pushed by the human to a
606→commit on `main` reuses `bundle.yml` and, from S onward, checks the workspace version against the
607→tag (B-016, wired in S; D-009).
608→
609→## 8. Deliverables
610→
611→Grown at every integration, never written at the end (rule 16).
612→
613→- **README.md**: what it is, the clean-clone commands (`make doctor`, `make check`, replay,
614→  `make app-dev`), the mission command of §2, the gate, the demo branch pair, honest time and
615→  usage per milestone (rule 10, from `reports/usage/`), what was left out with the reason.
616→- **docs/decisions/**: one file per decision, `make decisions-index` regenerates the README. The
617→  mission writes at least: mapping v1 and the `--tag`/child-session findings (M0), coverage
618→  component and threshold (S), machete (S), series allocation (M5 or earlier), demo branch pair
619→  superseding the private repo (M4), hybrid backlog (S), any model or effort change (rule 19), and
620→  the M1 go/no-go outcome.
621→- **BACKLOG.md and the hybrid backlog** (entry 19, mission-driven): at S integration the
622→  orchestrator creates GitHub issues labelled `backlog` from the open B-items of this spec, adds
623→  `scripts/gen-backlog.sh` that regenerates `BACKLOG.md` from the issues at every integration, and
624→  writes the decision file. Items the spec closed (B-005, B-007, B-010, B-014, B-017) are marked
625→  done with this spec as the reason. **Rule 14 wording** proposed for owner approval with this
626→  spec (RULES.md is the owner's): "everything else goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled
627→  `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`) with its reason". Until approved, `BACKLOG.md` stays the
628→  source and no issue is created.
629→- **build-log/**: one JSON line per tool call per session, written by the PostToolUse hook,
630→  committed with each integration (exempt from the 200 KB limit).
631→- **ai/session/**: one entry per interaction with transcript links; the mission appends to
632→  `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md` (or a dated successor) at every boundary.
633→- **reports/**: `usage/<m>.md` (tokens, credits, USD-eq per role and model, pasted),
634→  `waste/<m>.md` (from M5 onward, computed by the observatory on its own capture),
635→  `readiness/<date>-<m>.json` (B-015, every integration), `ci/<date>-<m>.md` (aggregate wall time),
636→  `reference/` (the owner's spreadsheet, B-008).
637→- **Spec PR** (before the mission): this file, the model-id corrections already in the working
638→  tree (entry 21), the three reasoning-effort keys in `.factory/settings.json`
639→  (`missionOrchestratorReasoningEffort = "high"`, `workerReasoningEffort = "high"`,
640→  `validationWorkerReasoningEffort = "high"`), session log entries 20–23, the PRD §13 M4 row and
641→  §14 risk row reworded to the demo branch pair, and BACKLOG B-007 reworded (entry 19), on a
642→  `docs/spec-v1` branch, PR to `main`, merged by the human. Reason: the mission command reads
643→  `SPEC.md` from the branch it starts on, and `main` is the only branch a mission starts from (§2).
644→
645→## 9. Changelog and human feedback
646→
647→Written by the orchestrator on the mission branch, never in a worktree.
648→
649→| Id | Date | Feedback | Applies | Status |
650→|---|---|---|---|---|
651→| F-001 | 2026-10-22 | Orchestrator model id is `claude-fable-5.1`, not `claude-fable-5-1` (fell back to GPT-6 Sol) | §2, D-006, settings, README, config, price table | done (spec PR) |

653→| F-003 | 2026-10-22 | Hybrid backlog is fine, the mission drives it | §8 | in spec, rule 14 wording awaiting approval |

## /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory/ai/RULES.md
# Rules

The rules this project inherits, adapted for a build run as a Factory Mission (orchestrator, workers, validators) with the human as owner. Derived from the artstudio set (14-oct-2026); rules that only made sense for a hand-run team are struck, not deleted, so the decision is visible.

1. **Tests before code.** No production code without a failing test that asks for it. Workers write the test first and commit it red; validators check that the red run exists in the log. Tests are the contract between the spec and the build.
2. **A walking skeleton first.** The thinnest end-to-end slice (core crate, canonical event model, `observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is on the mission branch before any milestone deepens its area, so every integration is checked by real acceptance tests.
3. **Versions verified, latest stable.** Every crate, tool and image is pinned to a version checked against the official source on the day it is added; the spec's version table says when.
4. **No secrets, no magic values.** Credentials only from the OS keychain or the environment, never in the repo, the store or the logs; every number (poll interval, stall threshold, price) comes from configuration with a stated default and a reason in the spec.
5. **Everything from a clean clone.** `cargo test`, `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay <fixture>` and the app build work on a machine that has only the Rust toolchain and the Tauri prerequisites; the README's commands are the ones CI runs.
6. **CI is a gate, not infrastructure.** Light checks on the mission branch: `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`, the replay fixtures, `cargo deny` (advisories and licences), gitleaks. The full attested run on the one pull request into `main`: everything above plus Semgrep (SAST), Trivy filesystem scan on `Cargo.lock`, Checkov on the workflows themselves, an SBOM (`syft` or `cargo-sbom`), the Tauri bundle built on macOS, build provenance with `actions/attest-build-provenance`, cosign-signed artifacts, with the Trivy results and the SBOM attached to the release. It never deploys.
7. **Counts come off the tool.** Test counts, timings, token usage and scan results are pasted from the run that produced them, never estimated.
8. **The spec is as-built.** When the code and the spec disagree at the end of a milestone, the spec is updated in the same integration, with the reason in `docs/decisions/`.
9. **Deviations are the human's to approve.** The orchestrator proposes, with reason and cost, and waits.
10. **Honest time.** The README states the real time and usage spent per milestone; what was left out is listed, not hidden.
11. **CI under three minutes warm on the mission branch.** Independent jobs in parallel, cargo and tool caches, prebuilt actions; the heavy stage only on the final pull request. Measured per run and reported.
12. **Git forward only, one PR per mission.** Never amend, reset, rebase or stash; a mistake is fixed by a new commit. Milestones live in worktrees and are integrated into `mission/<name>`; nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. A milestone is never shippable; the mission is.
13. **One file per decision, no shared files across worktrees.** `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` (what, why, alternatives, consequences); the index is generated. Two worktrees never edit the same file; the living spec sections are written by the orchestrator on the mission branch at integration time.
14. **Review fixes what blocks.** Blocking and security findings are fixed in the milestone, once; everything else goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`) with its reason. A review never starts a second round for style.
15. **Nothing reaches an agent mid-task.** Decisions are settled before a milestone starts; what comes up later waits for the next milestone or goes to the backlog. The human messages the mission only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up.
16. **Deliverables grow with the work.** README, decisions, backlog, build-log and the session log start with the skeleton and are extended at every integration, never written at the end.
17. **Everything is logged.** Hooks record every tool call to `build-log/`; every session transcript is linked from the session log; usage per model and per milestone is recorded. The build of the observatory is itself a dataset for the observatory.
18. **Unknown is surfaced, never dropped.** An event the mapper does not recognise is counted and shown; a milestone that adds a source ends with zero unknown events on its capture.
19. **Models per role are declared.** Orchestrator, worker and validator models are named in the spec and in the mission command; a change of model is a decision file.

Struck from the artstudio set: *tester, coder and reviewer as separate agents per team* (the Mission's workers and validators take those roles; if the validators prove weaker, custom sub-droids bring the split back, as a decision); *the 90-minute box* (replaced by usage budgets per milestone).

## /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory/.github/workflows/mission-branch.yml
# Light checks on mission branches (ai/RULES.md rules 6 and 11).
# Target: under three minutes warm. Independent jobs run in parallel; the
# aggregate job `mission-checks` is the single name other tooling depends on.
#
# Rust jobs activate automatically once Cargo.toml exists (walking skeleton).

name: mission-branch

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - "mission/**"
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - "mission/**"
  workflow_call:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: mission-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"

jobs:
  detect:
    name: detect
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    outputs:
      has_rust: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_rust }}
      has_fixtures: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_fixtures }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - id: probe
        run: |
          if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then echo "has_rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_rust=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          if ls fixtures/streams/*.jsonl >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "has_fixtures=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_fixtures=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

  docs:
    name: docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: markdownlint
        uses: DavidAnson/markdownlint-cli2-action@21c1be1b93ad9ed58fa840aacc3f279cde2a72ff # v24.2.0
        with:
          globs: "**/*.md"
      - name: decisions index is current
        run: make check-decisions-index
      - name: file size
        run: make check-file-size
      - name: debt markers reference an issue or backlog item
        run: make check-todos

  links:
    name: links
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

# The gate: the mission's single pull request into main (ai/RULES.md rules 6 and 12).
# Everything from mission-branch.yml plus SAST, filesystem scan, workflow policy,
# SBOM, the macOS Tauri bundle (bundle.yml), build provenance and cosign signatures.
# Semgrep and Trivy results are uploaded as SARIF to GitHub code scanning so
# findings appear on the PR and in the Security tab (BACKLOG B-013).
# It never deploys.
#
# `gate` is the aggregate job and the only required status check in the main
# ruleset (docs/decisions/D-003). Add jobs by appending them to its `needs`.

name: gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: gate-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"

jobs:
  detect:
    name: detect
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    outputs:
      has_rust: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_rust }}
      has_fixtures: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_fixtures }}
      has_tauri: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_tauri }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - id: probe
        run: |
          if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then echo "has_rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_rust=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          if ls fixtures/streams/*.jsonl >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "has_fixtures=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_fixtures=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          if [ -f apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json ]; then echo "has_tauri=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_tauri=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

  light:
    name: light
    uses: ./.github/workflows/mission-branch.yml
    permissions:
      contents: read

  sast:
    name: sast
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    container:
      image: semgrep/semgrep:1.182.0
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: semgrep
        run: semgrep scan --config p/default --config p/rust --config p/secrets --config p/github-actions --error --metrics=off --sarif --output semgrep.sarif
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: semgrep-results
          path: semgrep.sarif

  # Separate job: the codeql-action needs the runner's Node, which the semgrep
  # container does not provide.
  sast-upload:
    name: sast-upload
    needs: sast
    if: always() && needs.sast.result != 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: semgrep-results
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370 # v4.39.1
        with:
          sarif_file: semgrep.sarif
          category: semgrep

  fs-scan:
    name: fs-scan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: trivy filesystem scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@ed142fd0673e97e23eac54620cfb913e5ce36c25 # v0.36.0
        with:
          scan-type: fs
          scan-ref: .
          scanners: vuln,misconfig,secret
          severity: HIGH,CRITICAL
          exit-code: "1"
          ignore-unfixed: true
          format: sarif
          output: trivy-results.sarif
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: trivy-results
          path: trivy-results.sarif
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370 # v4.39.1
        if: always()
        with:
          sarif_file: trivy-results.sarif
          category: trivy

  workflow-policy:
    name: workflow-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: checkov on the workflows themselves
        uses: bridgecrewio/checkov-action@c3e106d5f8f4253a6de5110efb41a080f83db294 # v12
        with:
          directory: .github/workflows
          framework: github_actions
          soft_fail: false

  sbom:
    name: sbom
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: anchore/sbom-action@66cbf4bc1f1c0d2edc94016e65bc221b6bb0ad6c # v0.24.3
        with:
          path: .
          format: spdx-json
          artifact-name: sbom.spdx.json
          upload-artifact: true

  bundle:
    name: bundle
    needs: detect
    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_tauri == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/bundle.yml
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write

  gate:
    name: gate
    needs: [detect, light, sast, sast-upload, fs-scan, workflow-policy, sbom, bundle]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 1

# droid-observatory — single source of commands.
# README, AGENTS.md, .githooks and .github/workflows all call these targets,
# so a command documented is a command CI runs (ai/RULES.md rule 5).
#
# Rust targets are no-ops until the walking skeleton lands a Cargo.toml;
# they activate automatically, nothing here needs to change.

SHELL := /bin/sh
.DEFAULT_GOAL := help

HAS_CARGO := $(wildcard Cargo.toml)
HAS_TAURI := $(wildcard apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json)
HAS_FIXTURES := $(wildcard fixtures/streams/*.jsonl)

# Thresholds (ai/RULES.md rule 4: every number has a home and a reason).
# MAX_FILE_KB: source files over this are a review smell; captured stream fixtures are exempt.
MAX_FILE_KB ?= 200

.PHONY: help doctor hooks check check-docs check-links check-workflows check-file-size \
        check-todos check-decisions-index decisions-index check-secrets \
        fmt fmt-check lint test deny replay-fixtures build app-dev app-build clean

help: ## List targets
	@grep -E '^[a-zA-Z_-]+:.*?## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | awk 'BEGIN{FS=":.*?## "}{printf "  %-24s %s\n", $$1, $$2}'

doctor: ## Check local tools and print install hints
	@sh scripts/doctor.sh

hooks: ## Install git hooks (one-time after clone)
	@git config core.hooksPath .githooks && echo "hooks: core.hooksPath=.githooks"

# --- Light checks: run on every mission-branch push, must stay under 3 minutes warm ---

check: check-docs check-links check-workflows check-file-size check-todos check-decisions-index check-secrets fmt-check lint test deny replay-fixtures ## All light checks (= mission-branch CI)

check-docs: ## Lint markdown
	@markdownlint-cli2 "**/*.md"

check-links: ## Check links in markdown (needs network)
	@lychee --config lychee.toml --no-progress "**/*.md"

check-workflows: ## Lint GitHub workflows
	@actionlint

check-file-size: ## Fail on tracked files larger than MAX_FILE_KB
	@MAX_FILE_KB=$(MAX_FILE_KB) sh scripts/check-file-size.sh

check-todos: ## Debt markers must reference an issue (#123) or a backlog item (B-123)
	@sh scripts/check-todos.sh

decisions-index: ## Regenerate docs/decisions/README.md
	@sh scripts/gen-decisions-index.sh > docs/decisions/README.md

	@sh scripts/gen-decisions-index.sh | diff -u docs/decisions/README.md - \
	  || { echo "decisions index stale: run 'make decisions-index'"; exit 1; }

check-secrets: ## Scan the repository for committed secrets
	@gitleaks git --no-banner --redact .

# --- Rust (active once Cargo.toml exists) ---

fmt: ## Format Rust code
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo fmt --all
else
	@echo "fmt: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"
endif

fmt-check: ## Check Rust formatting
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo fmt --all -- --check
else
	@echo "fmt-check: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"
endif

lint: ## Clippy with warnings denied
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity
else
	@echo "lint: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"
endif

test: ## Run the test suite
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo test --workspace --all-features
else
	@echo "test: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"
endif

deny: ## cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans, sources
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo deny check
else
	@echo "deny: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"
endif

replay-fixtures: ## Replay every captured stream fixture through observatory-cli
ifneq (,$(HAS_FIXTURES))
	@for f in fixtures/streams/*.jsonl; do \
	  echo "replay $$f"; cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay "$$f" >/dev/null || exit 1; \
	done
else
	@echo "replay-fixtures: no fixtures/streams/*.jsonl yet, skipped"
endif

build: ## Build all crates (release)
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo build --workspace --release
else
	@echo "build: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"
endif

app-dev: ## Open the Tauri dev window
ifneq (,$(HAS_TAURI))
	@cargo tauri dev
else
	@echo "app-dev: no Tauri app yet, skipped"
endif

app-build: ## Build the Tauri desktop bundle (macOS)
ifneq (,$(HAS_TAURI))
	@cargo tauri build
else
	@echo "app-build: no Tauri app yet, skipped"
endif

clean: ## Remove build output
	@rm -rf target dist
